programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac air bhioran – an e àite draoidheil a tha seo? E fèir mìorbhaileach! Daolag-bhreac is excited - is this a magic place? It’s just amazing!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona and Baba plan a surprise for Mama and Papa - they're going to collect some lovely bright flowers for them! Baba comes across a honeybee in the meadow. Wherever bees are, there'll be flowers - they know where the best ones are! Oona, Baba and the bees find lots of beautiful flowers, but when they get to the Undergrowth, the Pufflings see more bees than they bargained for. Tha Oona is Baba ag ullachadh iongnadh 'son Mamaidh is Papaidh – 'ad a' dol a bhuain lusan breàgha, daiteach air an son! Tha Baba a' faicinn seillean-meala san achadh. Ge brith cà' bheil seilleanan, bidh lusan – fhios aca far a bheil an fheadhainn as fheàrr! Tha Oona, Baba agus na seilleanan a' lorg tòrr lusan àlainn, ach nuiar a ruigeas 'ad am Preaslach, tha na buthaidean a' faicinn barrachd sheilleanan na bha iad an dùil.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba can't wait for his swimming lesson, and he has a great instructor - his big sister Oona. She teaches Baba to paddle, steer with his feet, and put his head under the water. With some practice, and encouragement from Oona and Mama, Baba starts to get the hang of it - but diving proves much more difficult, until Lala drops a shiny shell in the water. Tha fadachd air Baba 'son an leasan snàimh aige, agus tha tidsear air leth aige – a phiuthar mhòr, Oona. Tha Oona a' teagasg grunnachadh do Bhaba, stiùireadh le spògan, agus a bhith a' cur a cheann fon uisge. Le beagan ullachaidh, 's le brosnachadh bho Oona is Mamaidh, tha Baba a' teannadh ri làmh an uachdair fhaighinn air cùisean – ach tha daibheadh fada nas dorra...gus an leag Lala slige dhealrach dhan uisge.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: ’S fìor thoil le Fuigheag a bhith falach air Boban is tha e coltach gu bheil Boban dèidheil air falach fead cuideachd! Fuigheag loves to hide from Boban and it turns out that Boban really enjoys falach fead, too.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Tha Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo gus innse dhaibh mu chuirm a chunnaic i. Tha seo gam brosnachadh gus cuirm shònraichte a chur air dòigh dhithse agus, às dèidh beagan ullachaidh, tha iad deiseil airson a thoirt chun an àrd-ùrlair. Linda visits her friend Meaban and Moo to tell them about her trip to the theatre. This gives them the idea to put on a concert for Linda and the stage is soon set for a very special performance!

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ còcaireachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Maya agus Anthony cuide ri Linda agus iad a’ fuine aran sòda. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad dèanamh cinnteach gu bheil na tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha min-fhlùir a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson aran sòda a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe! Linda Macleod and friends cook a number of tasty dishes. In this episode, Linda is joined by Maya and Anthony to make soda bread. Before they start, they must make sure they have all the ingredients and, if not, they prepare a list and go shopping. They also find out more about where flour comes from, before returning to the kitchen to bake the bread and sitting down at the table to tuck in.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Ailig Dòmhnallach a’ leughadh Nighean Bheag Chrosta a’ Chòta Dheirg. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Julia Jarman agus a dhealbhachadh le Jane Cope. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Mòrag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Alec MacDonald reads Nighean Bheag Chrosta a’ Chòta Dheirg, written by Julia Jarman, illustrated by Jane Cope and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella air a glacadh eadar Mia is Freya nuair a tha ‘ad ag argamaid. Ciamar a gheibh i fuasgladh air an trod gus am bi ‘ad air ais nan caraidean a-rithist Stella is caught between Mia and Freya when they argue. How will she find a solution to the fighting so that they will be friends again?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha Stella a’ coinneachadh ris an sgoilear iomlaid aice, Orla, chan eil cùisean a' dol cho math 's a bha i an dùil. Tha Orla caran nèonach. Ciamar a gheibh Stella ceangal eatarra gus am faigh iad air adhart le chèile? When Stella meets her exchange student, Orla, things don’t go as well as she’d hoped. Orla is a little strange. How will Stella find some kind of common bond so that they will get on well with each other?

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Bonns den bheachd gu bheil na Gumbalan mòra nas fheàrr air cleasan – ‘s e sin gus an do dh'fheuch i air an dùbhlan as dorra ‘Nas Fheàrr A-Mach Seach A-Steach’! Bounce thinks that the bigger Gumbles are better at tricks - that is until she tries the most difficult challenge ‘Better Out Than In’!

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Tha seann teampall falaichte le ìomhaighean annasach na dhìomhaireas do Na Neachdan an-diugh. Às bi dè eile, an aire air na freiceadanan! A strange hidden ancient temple with unusual statues is a mystery to the Neachdan today. Whatever else, beware the sentinels!

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Kate comes across an interesting sea creature, known as a sunfish, which is native to tropical waters but is likely to have been carried to the islands by the Gulf Stream.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Calum Maclean is in Glasgow taking a step back in time along the banks of the River Clyde. We also meet learners Audrey and Davy Paterson from Taynuilt.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le The Poozies le Wired to the Moon agus Sausage. Clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Concert set performed by The Poozies, featuring the tracks Wired to the Moon and Sausage. Originally recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: Murdina confronts Johan with CCTV evidence of the hotel fire. Sìleas hatches a plan to save the mill, while Seumas make a sacrifice that could leave him with nothing. Still reeling from the aftermath of the ‘Reul na Mara’ fire, Cairistiona makes a big decision. Anns an earrann mu dheireadh dhen t-sreath, tha Murdina a’ dol aghaidh ri aghaidh ri Johan leis an fhianais CCTV a th’ aice dhen teine san taigh-òsta. Tha Sìleas a’ cur roimhpe a’ mhuileann a shàbhaileadh fhad ‘s a tha Seumas a’ dèanamh ìobairt a dh’fhaodadh fhàgail gun chàil idir. Fhathast a’ feuchainn ri faighinn seachad air an teine ann an ‘Reul na Mara’, tha Cairistìona a’ tighinn gu co-dhùnadh mòr. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Cùram
programme.desc: Tha sinn a’ coinneachadh ri Dòmhnall Iain MacIlleathain à Solas ann an Uibhist a Tuath, aig a bheil cerebral palsy. We meet Donald John Maclean from Sollas in North Uist who has cerebral palsy.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke forage at the shore for razor clams, kelp lasagne and carrageen dessert.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Prògram aithriseach ciùil le Julie Fowlis is Muireann NicAmhlaoibh. Nì Port taisbeanadh air na ceanglaichean dualchais a tha eadar an dithis aca. An t-seachdain-sa tha Julie agus Muireann a' tadhal air Siorrachd Chiarri agus còmhla riutha, tha dithis a Alba; an sàr sheinneadair Seumas Greumach agus a neach-ciùil barraichte, Iain MacPhàrlain a Gleann Fhionnain. Bha Siorrachd Chiarri a-riamh ainmeil airson luchd-ciùil agus tha na seòid a'coinneachadh ris na chòmlain Lumiere agus Cuas; agus ri Pádraig Ó Sé airson còmhradh agus, gu nadurrach, airson stùr a chuir a puirt. Musical documentary presented by Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh. Port reveals their shared musical heritage and in this episode Julie and Muireann visit Co Kerry. Accompanying them from Scotland are renowned singer James Graham and the brilliant Glennfinnan musician, Iain MacFarlane. The south west of Ireland and Co Kerry have long been noted for the calibre of their musicians - we meet the bands Lumiere and Cuas, plus Pádraig Ó Sé for some craic and lively musical sessions.

programme.title: Kathleen
programme.desc: Tha am prògram seo a’deanamh luaidh air an t-seinneadair Ghàidhlig Kathleen NicAonghais, à Uibhist a Deas, a tha air a bhith a’ cosnadh cliù dhith fhèin anns a West End ann an Lunnainn, a’ seinn anns an dealbh-cliuch chliùiteach ‘MacBheatha’ aig Taighcluiche Harold Pinter. Tha an guth-seinn aig Kathleen beairteach ann an traidisean, agus ri linn sin, a’ còrdadh ri luchd-èisteachdan fad is farsuinn. Bheiridh am prògram seo tarraing air an turas ciùil aig Kathleen, a’ sgrùdadh a freumhan domhainn ann an cultar na Gàidhlig, agus a’ taisbeanadh measgachadh de phìosan tasglainn bho seinn gu cleasachd air Tbh. This documentary celebrates the career of Gaelic singer Kathleen MacInnes, a captivating performer from South Uist whose talent has brought her to the heights of London’s West End. Fresh from starring in the acclaimed production of ‘Macbeth’ at the Harold Pinter Theatre, Kathleen’s voice, rich in tradition, resonates with audiences far and wide. The programme delves into her musical journey, explores her deep roots in Gaelic culture, and showcases rare archival footage from her diverse singing and TV acting career. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Tha na seòid a’ cruthachadh reasabaidhean às aonais chruithneachd no bathar-bainne. Wheat and dairy intolerance is widespread, the lads come up with healthy alternatives.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Sylvia Syms looks at the handsome heroes and gorgeous heroines, pin-ups and bombshells who came to be known as cinema's greatest sex symbols. They were the actors who made audiences' hearts beat fastest - the men and women whom the camera just seemed to love that little bit more than most. The programme hears from the stars themselves talking about what their sex symbol status meant to them, and the good-looking line-up includes Gary Cooper, Jane Russell, Brigitte Bardot, Paul Newman, Robert Redford and Hollywood's ultimate sex symbol, Marilyn Monroe.

programme.title: Eve and Marilyn
programme.desc: 'She had a total understanding and control of the still camera... she was intelligent enough and sharp enough and beautiful enough to be able to manipulate almost any situation, so it became something which was totally her own...' Eve Arnold, one of the world's leading photo-journalists, remembers photographing Marilyn Monroe over the ten crucial years of Marilyn's stardom and decline. Going back to the original contact sheets and colour material, she tells of their friendship and what it was like as a woman to photograph Marilyn Monroe.

programme.title: Scene by Scene
programme.desc: A rare interview with former Hollywood sex symbol Jane Russell. She talks about her difficult childhood as the eldest and only girl of six siblings, her film career and working with Marilyn Monroe.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: It’s the penultimate match of the first round. Newnham College, Cambridge, face the Courtauld Institute of Art for a place in the second round. Jeremy Paxman asks the questions.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Semi-final of the quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take players so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. It is all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: India: Nature's Wonderland
programme.desc: The hidden wonders of India's spectacular natural world are revealed by wildlife expert Liz Bonnin, actress Freida Pinto and mountaineer Jon Gupta. Experience a village of birds, masks that come alive, the world's greatest mountain range and baby turtles erupting out of the sand. This is truly a land like no other.

programme.title: Art of Scandinavia
programme.desc: In the final instalment of Andrew Graham-Dixon's windswept journey through the art of the Norselands, we arrive in Sweden - home of Ikea and a tradition of brilliant furniture design stretching back to the early years of the 20th century. Sweden has made its modern democratic mission one of comfort and civilised living for the masses - but has it got there?

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes charts the foundation of a national identity that sought architectural inspiration from Greece and Rome. He also looks at America's earliest major painters.

programme.title: Art That Made Us
programme.desc: An explosion of new voices from across the British Isles reinvents the arts, creating a richer, more diverse culture.

programme.title: King Otto and Football’s Greek Gods
programme.desc: In the summer of 2004, audiences looked on in disbelief as the Greek national football team, who had never previously won a single match or even scored a goal in a major tournament, took down the giants of world football to become the unlikeliest of European champions. The architect behind this unprecedented triumph was legendary German football coach ‘King’ Otto Rehhagel. After accomplishing every major success in Germany, he made the bold decision to leave all he knew behind and work in a foreign country with the underachieving Greek national team. This is the story of how these two contrasting cultures came together to speak the same language and write a new chapter of Greek mythology.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded examines a dramatic week for Elon Musk that could reshape the future of artificial intelligence. A US court has rejected Musk's claims against OpenAI, bringing a long-running feud with co-founder Sam Altman into sharp focus and offering a rare glimpse inside one of the world's most influential AI companies. At the same time, SpaceX is preparing for what could be the largest stock market listing in history - a move that may value the company at up to $1.75 trillion and make Musk the world's first human trillionaire.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from urban Hertfordshire with a £550,000 budget have their sights set on moving to the Somerset countryside, where Jules Hudson has some splendid properties lined up to tempt them. However, Jules has a big surprise up his sleeve, as he questions not the type of new home they’re looking for but the location of it.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns, but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Rose Matafeo. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. As the pressure to win increases, Pippa Grange questions her role. Meanwhile, Gareth tries to unite a divided country ahead of Euro 2020, where he hopes the team finally bring it home at Wembley.

programme.title: Arthur the King
programme.desc: Over the course of ten days and 435 miles, an unbreakable bond is forged between pro adventure racer Michael Light and a scrappy street dog companion dubbed Arthur. Desperate for one last chance to win, Michael convinces a sponsor to back him and a team of athletes for the Adventure Racing World Championship in the Dominican Republic. As the team is pushed to their outer limits of endurance in the race, Arthur redefines what victory, loyalty and friendship truly mean. Based on a true story.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. As the pressure to win increases, Pippa Grange questions her role. Meanwhile, Gareth tries to unite a divided country ahead of Euro 2020, where he hopes the team finally bring it home at Wembley.

programme.title: Arthur the King

As the team is pushed to their outer limits of endurance in the race, Arthur redefines what victory, loyalty and friendship truly mean. Based on a true story.

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from urban Hertfordshire with a £550,000 budget have their sights set on moving to the Somerset countryside, where Jules Hudson has some splendid properties lined up to tempt them. However, Jules has a big surprise up his sleeve, as he questions not the type of new home they’re looking for but the location of it.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Arthur the King
programme.desc: Over the course of ten days and 435 miles, an unbreakable bond is forged between pro adventure racer Michael Light and a scrappy street dog companion dubbed Arthur. Desperate for one last chance to win, Michael convinces a sponsor to back him and a team of athletes for the Adventure Racing World Championship in the Dominican Republic. As the team is pushed to their outer limits of endurance in the race, Arthur redefines what victory, loyalty and friendship truly mean. Based on a true story.

programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from urban Hertfordshire with a £550,000 budget have their sights set on moving to the Somerset countryside, where Jules Hudson has some splendid properties lined up to tempt them. However, Jules has a big surprise up his sleeve, as he questions not the type of new home they’re looking for but the location of it.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns, but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Rose Matafeo. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Max confronts the Mitchells about his suspicions, Gina gives Eddie the cold shoulder, and Zack gets some unwelcome news.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. As the pressure to win increases, Pippa Grange questions her role. Meanwhile, Gareth tries to unite a divided country ahead of Euro 2020, where he hopes the team finally bring it home at Wembley.

programme.title: Carl Frampton - On Probation
programme.desc: Carl is back with probation officer Toni, who finds out one of her service users is about to become a father again. Carl follows the story as Toni puts measures into place to safeguard the progress the service user has made. Meanwhile in Belfast, Carl meets a woman who successfully completed probation and has big plans for her future, but her struggles with alcohol continue to hang over her.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? programme.title: Carl Frampton - On Probation
programme.desc: Carl is back with probation officer Toni, who finds out one of her service users is about to become a father again. He is on probation for serious assault and has an historic conviction for assault on a former partner. Carl follows the story as Toni puts measures into place to safeguard the progress the service user has made. But his past conviction catches up with him and threatens to derail him if he doesn’t make serious changes. Meanwhile in Belfast, Carl meets a woman who successfully completed probation and has big plans for her future, but her struggles with alcohol continue to hang over her.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong hosts, with guest panellists Phil Wang and Judi Love joining team captains Ian and Paul as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Arthur the King
programme.desc: Over the course of ten days and 435 miles, an unbreakable bond is forged between pro adventure racer Michael Light and a scrappy street dog companion dubbed Arthur. Desperate for one last chance to win, Michael convinces a sponsor to back him and a team of athletes for the Adventure Racing World Championship in the Dominican Republic. As the team is pushed to their outer limits of endurance in the race, Arthur redefines what victory, loyalty and friendship truly mean. Based on a true story.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns, but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Rose Matafeo. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from urban Hertfordshire with a £550,000 budget have their sights set on moving to the Somerset countryside, where Jules Hudson has some splendid properties lined up to tempt them. However, Jules has a big surprise up his sleeve, as he questions not the type of new home they’re looking for but the location of it.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns, but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Rose Matafeo. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Max confronts the Mitchells about his suspicions, Gina gives Eddie the cold shoulder, and Zack gets some unwelcome news.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. As the pressure to win increases, Pippa Grange questions her role. Meanwhile, Gareth tries to unite a divided country ahead of Euro 2020, where he hopes the team finally bring it home at Wembley.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from urban Hertfordshire with a £550,000 budget have their sights set on moving to the Somerset countryside, where Jules Hudson has some splendid properties lined up to tempt them. However, Jules has a big surprise up his sleeve, as he questions not the type of new home they’re looking for but the location of it.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Max confronts the Mitchells about his suspicions, Gina gives Eddie the cold shoulder, and Zack gets some unwelcome news.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. programme.title: Arthur the King
programme.desc: Over the course of ten days and 435 miles, an unbreakable bond is forged between pro adventure racer Michael Light and a scrappy street dog companion dubbed Arthur. Desperate for one last chance to win, Michael convinces a sponsor to back him and a team of athletes for the Adventure Racing World Championship in the Dominican Republic. As the team is pushed to their outer limits of endurance in the race, Arthur redefines what victory, loyalty and friendship truly mean. Based on a true story.

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Arthur the King

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: The Scarecrows' Wedding
programme.desc: An enchanting story about two devoted scarecrows, Betty O’Barley and Harry O’Hay, who are planning a wedding to remember. When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from urban Hertfordshire with a £550,000 budget have their sights set on moving to the Somerset countryside, where Jules Hudson has some splendid properties lined up to tempt them. However, Jules has a big surprise up his sleeve, as he questions not the type of new home they’re looking for but the location of it.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns, but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Rose Matafeo. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.
