When Harry insists on leaving the farm to collect one last thing for their big day, a smooth-talking scarecrow named Reginald Rake swoops in with plans of his own. Chaos ensues, and soon, Betty is in danger and everything’s at risk. Can Harry get back in time and save the day? Full of heart, humour and adventure, this is the joyful tale about loyalty, love and learning that the most important thing isn’t a grand gesture – it’s simply being together. This half-hour animated special features an all-star voice cast with returning favourite Rob Brydon (Gavin and Stacey, The Trip) voicing Reginald Rake, Jessie Buckley (Wicked Little Letters, Wild Rose) as Betty O’Barley and Domhnall Gleeson (About Time, The Paper) as Harry O’Hay, all led by Sophie Okonedo (Slow Horses, Hotel Rwanda) as the narrator.

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team investigate the fake bank accounts all registered in one Cheshire street and ask whether the bank responsible does enough to stop scammers opening accounts. Also on the programme, the woman who received a £600 high-end smartphone as a gift, only to discover it was counterfeit – and the online retail giant that wouldn’t refund her. And the quick-witted viewer who recorded a scam call and kept the criminals talking so he could expose their breathtaking tactics.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is charmed by a 19th-century cottage just outside Birmingham, and in particular the old-fashioned phone left behind. There is plenty of room for Tommy to park at a row of garages in London, and Jacqui is in Ipswich, where a tiny shower just off the kitchen can’t be passed off as being quirky!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha learns about England’s oldest biscuit, and the reds and blues shop for bargains in Nottinghamshire. Which team will have the recipe for success?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson spends this weekend break in the company of sporting legend Steve Cram. The middle-distance runner and broadcaster joins Robson on a boat trip from Seahouses to the Farne Islands to watch seals and seabirds. The duo take to the beach to sample the practice of ‘walking meditation’ as they create labyrinths in the sand. The mini break ends in a session of green woodworking at a bush craft site near Northumberland National Park.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from urban Hertfordshire with a £550,000 budget have their sights set on moving to the Somerset countryside, where Jules Hudson has some splendid properties lined up to tempt them. However, Jules has a big surprise up his sleeve, as he questions not the type of new home they’re looking for but the location of it.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: The team take on two gardens. Charlie and Amelia are in Stockport to transform Christine and Mike’s unloved plot into a glamorous art deco, 1920’s-themed garden, dripping in Hollywood sophistication with a nod to California, its palm trees and exotic planting. Flo and Lee are in Bristol to convert Emi and Song’s awkwardly shaped wrap-around garden into a Japanese-British fusion garden. They would love the garden to draw on their combined Japanese and British heritage, so it’s a mix of planting with cherry trees, acers from Japan and English roses, with areas for their children to play, grow vegetables and socialise.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jamie, Liam, Jack and Dan – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns, but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Rose Matafeo. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie goes back to the classroom, inspired by caring for her dad. Nerves hit on day one, but her first on-the-job work placement has a real impact.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Max confronts the Mitchells about his suspicions, Gina gives Eddie the cold shoulder, and Zack gets some unwelcome news.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Mike and Alison welcome the very first guests to their new bijoux B&B, determined to get a glowing review, whatever the cost. While serving the couple breakfast, Alison realises that they are not enjoying their anniversary break and, fearing a bad review, utilises the surprising skills of Lady Button and Julian to ensure the couple make the most of their weekend away. Mary reveals she has never had a holiday, so Pat tells her about the joys and pitfalls of week on the Costa Del Sol. Thomas is perplexed yet secretly thrilled by sudden attention from the Plaguers, who, after admiring Alison’s discarded portrait of him in the basement, are now affording him celebrity status in Button House, hanging on his every word. The Captain is outraged by this meaningless reverence, believing that only a handful of great war leaders deserve such unadulterated veneration. As he and Thomas clash over the Plaguers, he challenges them to endure a poetry recital in order to test their loyalty.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Dear England
programme.desc: After a breakthrough World Cup reignites belief, the England team return to a tournament on home turf, amidst the Covid pandemic. As the pressure to win increases, Pippa Grange questions her role. Meanwhile, Gareth tries to unite a divided country ahead of Euro 2020, where he hopes the team finally bring it home at Wembley.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong hosts, with guest panellists Phil Wang and Judi Love joining team captains Ian and Paul as they delve into the news.

programme.title: Arthur the King
programme.desc: Over the course of ten days and 435 miles, an unbreakable bond is forged between pro adventure racer Michael Light and a scrappy street dog companion dubbed Arthur. Desperate for one last chance to win, Michael convinces a sponsor to back him and a team of athletes for the Adventure Racing World Championship in the Dominican Republic. As the team is pushed to their outer limits of endurance in the race, Arthur redefines what victory, loyalty and friendship truly mean. Based on a true story.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Scotland boasts some of the very best public gardens in the UK. We visit a selection of Scottish gardens that are open to the public but we are given personal, and sometimes behind-the-scenes, tours of these lovely places. Kirsty shows the hidden living roof at the Royal Botanic Gardens Edinburgh, Brian gives insight into Scone Palace’s hedge maze, and at Branklyn Gardens in Perth we are treated to the gardener’s tour.

programme.title: The Harbour
programme.desc: Aberdeen Harbour, on the North East coast of Scotland, is one of Britain's oldest businesses and one of Europe's most modern ports. It is the heartbeat of the offshore oil and gas industry. Every year, more than eight thousand boats pass through the harbour waters, helped by the hidden world of the men and women who keep it running 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. This is their story... This week, we're with the crew of the ferry as it loads up then sails north for Orkney and Shetland. With over 380 passengers aboard, there are a lot hungry mouths to feed. In the boatman's bothy, the talk is also of food. Billy Duguid loves two things; a plate of scallops fresh from the North Sea and winding up colleague Craig Massie over their Torry v Footdee rivalry. And the stork arrives in the harbour not once but twice as pilots Tim Wingate and Jeff Gaskin both welcome new arrivals to their families.

programme.title: The Harbour
programme.desc: Aberdeen Harbour, on the north east coast of Scotland, is one of Britain's oldest businesses and one of Europe's most modern ports. It is the heartbeat of the offshore oil and gas industry. Every year, more than eight thousand boats pass through the harbour waters, helped by the hidden world of the men and women who keep it running 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. This is their story... In this, the final programme of the series, the dockers at Sea Cargo find themselves at the mercy of the weather as they race to prepare a vessel for a six-week voyage to West Africa. If sailing is delayed, costs will escalate by thousands. It's man overboard for boatman Billy Duguid as he volunteers for some RNLI training in the freezing North Sea. And a cruise ship full of Swedes headed for Balmoral sails in, while the harbour also hosts a ship's christening where all the pressure is on the godmother...

programme.desc: A surgeon must remove part of his patient’s tongue and reconstruct it to save her from an aggressive cancer, and surgeons perform a rare simultaneous pancreas and kidney transplant.

programme.title: Only Child
programme.desc: Ken forces Richard to accompany him to Aviemore so that he can help him navigate the QR code scanner at the train station ticket barrier. However, a mix-up on the platform turns what should be a simple day trip into an almighty fiasco.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Beth and Cathy think they are doing their good deed for the day when they drop Christine off at the hospital reception, but while Cathy manages to slip away, poor Beth doesn't get off so lightly and is committed to a visit post-op. With a long list of demands from Christine, Beth and Eric return later with her supplies to find that instead of being sore and exhausted after surgery, she has been sleeping off her dinner. It emerges the operation has been postponed until the following morning. As nurse Heather weathers Christine's demands, Colin arrives followed by Michelle and Alan. The ensuing group discussion leaves Christine very worried about her chances of survival.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: In Dumfries and Galloway, Nick and his wife, Holly, prepare to take over the family-run farm from his dad, Derek, who plans to retire later in the year. Nick wants to change how his father has been farming for over 30 years. He is experimenting with a breed of low-maintenance sheep that he believes are the future, but Derek is yet to be convinced. It's a critical year for Andy and Jo in Fife, who have taken out a £2-million loan to get into arable farming. Crops now account for 60 per cent of their income, but record-breaking rain could have a catastrophic impact on their wheat fields. They must wait for the frost to thaw to reveal the extent of the damage. The remote island Papa Westray is home to the Baker family, who moved there six years ago. New to farming, they rely on support from the community. In return, they do Friday night fish and chip takeaways, but the island’s dinner hangs in the balance as winter weather takes over.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie visits Bee Edge Farm near Eyemouth to help open the barn doors and let the cows out for summer. Continuing to mark Landward’s 50th anniversary, Cammy catches up with a farming pioneer who was never one for sitting on the fence, and Rosie is stepping back in time in Aberdeenshire to find out what one old farm building can tell us about our agricultural past. Elsewhere, Leanna is on the trail of a walrus that has been turning up in harbours around Scotland's north coast.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cuningham show how to help the pollinators in your garden and at Beechgrove as they focus on planting that will attract bees to your plot. Even if you don’t have a garden, Kirsty demonstrates how you can help the local ecosystem by sowing a meadow in a pot. She also discusses the best summer bulbs to plant now for fragrance and colour. Brian is back in the vegetable plot for his summer-long guide to productive gardening for beginners, and there is a demonstration of how to prune spring-flowering shrubs. All that and the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy is hopeful that he could be fighting again soon, and he and Molly-Mae are spending more time together, so things are finally looking up for him. Then, disaster strikes when KSI cancels the night when Roman was due to be in the fighting, claiming illness. John is furious but decides the boys need cheering up so tells them he is taking them on a camping trip. Neither Tommy nor Roman share their father’s love of the outdoors but do their best to enjoy a night under canvas. Tommy is beginning to redecorate the house in the hope that Molly-Mae may move back in, and he does his first red carpet event since the break-up. At the event, he reveals that Molly has agreed to go on a trial family holiday with him to Dubai. Could they be returning reunited?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy and Jake are heading to Budapest to shoot a promo and hopefully finally close the deal for his next fight. After 18 months out of action, Tommy will return to the ring, and he can’t wait to get back to what he does best. Even better, brother Roman will be fighting on the undercard, so both the Fury brothers will be in the ring on the same night. Back in Cheshire, work on the house continues in preparation for Molly’s return. Meanwhile, Tommy has precious time with Bambi before he has to leave her to go into fight camp. On the day Tommy is supposed to be flying to Hungary to start training, the money still hasn’t reached his account, so John calls everything off. Four days later, the money has finally landed, and the boys are in Budapest, training hard in fight camp. On a rare day off, we discover the importance of faith for the Fury boys and how in particular it has helped Tommy through his tough times. On Easter weekend, Tommy is reunited with Bambi for the last time before he gets into the ring - will his hand survive the fight?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: It is Tommy’s birthday, but there is no time for cake. With just days to go before his long-awaited comeback fight in Budapest, Tommy is pulled in every direction, juggling press conferences, promo shoots and the pressure of proving he has still got what it takes in the ring. Fighting on the same bill as his older brother Roman, Tommy steps into the spotlight once again and puts himself to the test against a hard-hitting Bosnian heavyweight. In a high-stakes bout that could define his future, Tommy isn’t just fighting for his career - he is fighting for the life he is desperate to rebuild. Meanwhile, there is a more personal battle quietly playing out at home. With the house freshly prepared for Molly-Mae and Bambi’s return, Tommy hopes he has done enough to prove he has changed. But now that he may have won them back, can he keep them?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: After the success of his comeback fight, Tommy’s road to redemption hits a major setback - his hand is injured again and needs eight weeks’ total rest before doctors will know if he can fight again. The last time he couldn’t train, his life spiralled out of control, so now Tommy throws himself into a frenzy of activity: a TV appearance on The Wheel, family days out with Bambi, and a final push to finish the home he hopes Molly and Bambi will soon return to. In search of focus and inspiration, Tommy heads to Marbella to train with his childhood hero - legendary bodybuilder Dorian Yates. But in a world of yacht trips, sun-soaked distractions and luxury villas, can Tommy stay disciplined and keep his relationship and boxing career back on track? As doubts grow over his recovery, Tommy faces the toughest question of all - is this just a setback or the beginning of the end of his boxing career?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy’s recovery is back on track after he and John put his hand to the test. The pair are training again, and the search for Tommy’s next opponent begins. Eager to make the most of family time, Tommy splashes out on a £90,000 motor home for family trips with Molly and Bambi and takes his mum out for lunch and a long-overdue catch-up. Tommy reveals that John has had a recent health scare, so to cheer him up, father and son take their very different caravans to a local steam fair. It’s vital for Tommy’s mental health that he keeps physically active at all times, so he sets his sights on an ambitious new goal - a 100km triathlon. Meanwhile, John worries that the physical toll from this could jeopardise the chances of Tommy recovering and landing a big money fight. As Tommy throws himself into training for the triathlon, one question remains - can he avoid getting injured, or will this new challenge end his boxing career for good?

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve and a team of world-class kayakers head to the Kamchatka Peninsula in the far east of Russia to take on the first descent of the Kronotsky River – through white water so extreme that it has never before been attempted. The team set out to paddle from source to sea, starting in the shadow of a still-active volcano and ending at the Pacific Ocean – kayaking through an unspoilt wilderness packed with more brown bears than almost anywhere else on the planet. If the team can make it through the white water, they will enter an untouched landscape and witness brown bears in their natural habitat, unaffected by humans. These Russian brown bears are so isolated, some of them may never have seen people before.

programme.title: The Cage
programme.desc: As forces close in on Matty and Leanne, and the evidence stacks up against them, can they pull off one last roll of the dice?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin lead the search along with guest judge and keen gardener Katie Piper to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. Up first is Colin’s surprising suburban rustic garden in suburban Ballymena. In the foothills of the Sperrin Mountains, near the windswept Glenshane Pass, Adrienne has transformed two acres using a variety of planting styles. The final stop is in Dromore, where Julietta has created a garden designed with her young family very much in mind, including a wild meadow playground and a courtyard filled with edible plants. There are mixed opinions at the judging table – so which will expert judges Diarmuid, Carol and Katie feel deserves a place in the Greatest Garden final?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Roman Kemp is ‘soaking up’ life in Glasgow, where children’s entertainer Susan is desperate for a good night’s sleep. Luckily, Roman has packed his rubber ducky – and some science. Adding a hot bath to your evening routine has been shown to help improve sleep, reduce the risk of heart disease and even burn a few extra calories. Relaxation with real results.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of the final day of the Premier League season's ten matches, including Arsenal’s trip to Crystal Palace and Manchester City versus Aston Villa. Elsewhere, Spurs host Everton, and West Ham welcome Leeds to the London Stadium. Presented by Kelly Cates, with Alan Shearer and Wayne Rooney.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie hosts as another four contenders take to the black chair, answering questions on their chosen specialist subjects to earn a place in the semi-finals. The specialist subjects are Michael Palin's travel documentaries, Lady Gaga, Emily Dickinson and the BBC sitcom Mum.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions while our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Louis’s reunion with his family is underwhelming, while at Oakley, Daisy's plans to have the vineyard represented in the Behind the Vines showcase receive a mixed response from Gus and Tippy. Daisy approaches Hilary and Nic for information on the event but is not entirely thrilled with what she learns. Tippy struggles with her confidence, while Gus’s inability to master the art of the haggle leads Daisy to a negotiation with the attractive Ben, only to discover she may be flirting with the enemy. Meanwhile, at Oakley, disaster hits when Rowan, Julian and Paige wreak havoc, and the reaction from a livid Louis leads Julian to a rash decision. Louis seeks advice from Daisy on how to repair his relationship with Simone, only to disregard it after further conversation with Gus. Full of high hopes, he plans a grand gesture but doesn’t receive the response he hopes for. Don offers Louis the drunken advice of an unwise man, which leads to an intoxicated declaration. And a conversation with Julian yields information that surprises Daisy, leading her to offer relationship advice to Simone, which leaves Louis less than impressed.

programme.title: Sicily: The Wonder of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Historian Michael Scott begins his journey through Sicily on the slopes of Mount Etna, Europe's largest active volcano. For the ancient Greeks, the island was a land of gods and monsters - a dangerous and unpredictable world. Michael discovers how 3,000 years ago, the Greeks began to settle on Sicily's east coast - planting their olives and vines and building great city-states that soon came to rival even Athens itself. He learns how great battles were fought between the Greeks and the Carthaginians for control of the island. How the Romans made it their first foreign colony and stripped Sicily of its forests to plant vast fields of grain. When Rome fell, waves of Barbarian invasions followed, before Sicily was conquered by the Byzantines - the eastern Roman Empire. How have those early invaders helped to shape the character of the island we see today? And what lessons have Sicilians learnt from their turbulent past?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. This show comes from Tidworth in Wiltshire, where fascinating finds include rare French porcelain, a regimental silver centrepiece, valuable toys and an unusual sardine tin.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: In Muncaster in Cumbria, hundreds of people turn up with collectibles and treasures they want to take to auction. Antiques experts James Lewis and Caroline Hawley uncover a few gems including a dazzling decanter and an art nouveau picture frame. Paul Martin visits Coniston Water in the Lake District.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael boards the Eurostar at London’s St Pancras International, bound for the Belgian capital, Brussels. In the city centre’s sumptuous Theatre Royal, he learns how an impassioned opera performance led to revolution on the streets and the birth of an independent nation. Travelling by tram to the residential district of Saint Gilles, Michael discovers the Belgian origins of art nouveau at the elegant house of architect Victor Horta. Finishing his first day at the headquarters of Nato, opened in 1967, he recalls his time as defence secretary and enjoys a private viewing of its impressive archive.

programme.title: Digging for Britain
programme.desc: In this special, Professor Alice Roberts reveals the forgotten story of the Roman Army's secret weapon in Britain - their cavalry. These fearsome horsemen were the key to defending Britain's most famous Roman monument fortification, Hadrian's Wall. Alice sets off across Hadrian's Wall to investigate any evidence the Roman cavalry left behind, while a team of archaeologists and historical re-enactors attempt to restage a Roman cavalry tournament - a spectacle that no-one has seen for over 1,600 years. We follow the team's training as they prepare for the performance, and Alice joins them at a public display in Carlisle where 30 riders perform in front of a crowd of spectators. To put the cavalry's story in context, the film also explores the latest archaeological digs happening across the UK, each of which is searching for new evidence of the Roman cavalry. On her journey across Hadrian's Wall, Alice visits some of the most iconic sites associated with the Roman cavalry, including Chester's Roman fort, Vindolanda fort and museum and Hexham Abbey. Along the way she builds a picture of the horsemen's lives here on the northern frontier of the Roman Empire.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Springwatch returns for three weeks of seasonal splendour. Broadcasting live from the brand new location of National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan deliver all the wildlife drama spring has to offer. With remote cameras rigged across the site, they uncover stories unfolding in real time. Iolo Williams undertakes his own wildlife wanderings, broadcasting live from the Knepp Estate in Sussex, where wildlife is thriving and ‘stand-out’ species are returning to the landscape.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy explores how the battle for American independence wasn’t only fought on American soil but also unfolded in Britain itself, with sabotage, espionage and political unrest reshaping the empire. She reflects on a revolution that created an independent America but which also reshaped Britain and its monarchy.

programme.title: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret.
programme.desc: Eleven-year-old Margaret is uprooted from her life in New York City for the suburbs of New Jersey, going through the messy and tumultuous throes of puberty with new friends in a new school. She relies on her mother, Barbara, who is also struggling to adjust to life outside the big city, and her adoring grandmother, Sylvia, who isn’t happy they moved away and likes to remind them every chance she gets. Based on Judy Blume’s classic novel.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani and Joe Crowley explore the River Leven, which flows through Fife, uncovering how this once hard-working industrial river shaped communities for centuries and how it’s now being transformed for the future. Anita joins archaeologists on a major new excavation digging into the river’s hidden past, before meeting the people helping to reconnect local communities with the water for the first time in generations. At Loch Leven, Joe gets hands-on with one of the river’s last working sluices to discover how its waters powered industry and why it still plays an important role today. He also joins scientists involved in one of the UK’s longest-running lake research programmes, monitoring the health of the river at its source. Meanwhile, on Adam Henson’s farm in the Cotswolds, annual spring plant surveys reveal how the landscape is changing year by year.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: After more than 11,000km across eight countries, the teams face one final test of endurance as they race to claim victory at the finish line in Hatgal, Mongolia.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve and a team of world-class kayakers head to the Kamchatka Peninsula in the far east of Russia to take on the first descent of the Kronotsky River – through white water so extreme that it has never before been attempted. The team set out to paddle from source to sea, starting in the shadow of a still-active volcano and ending at the Pacific Ocean – kayaking through an unspoilt wilderness packed with more brown bears than almost anywhere else on the planet. If the team can make it through the white water, they will enter an untouched landscape and witness brown bears in their natural habitat, unaffected by humans. These Russian brown bears are so isolated, some of them may never have seen people before.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie hosts as another four contenders take to the black chair, answering questions on their chosen specialist subjects to earn a place in the semi-finals. The specialist subjects are Michael Palin's travel documentaries, Lady Gaga, Emily Dickinson and the BBC sitcom Mum.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions while our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Louis’s reunion with his family is underwhelming, while at Oakley, Daisy's plans to have the vineyard represented in the Behind the Vines showcase receive a mixed response from Gus and Tippy. Daisy approaches Hilary and Nic for information on the event but is not entirely thrilled with what she learns. Tippy struggles with her confidence, while Gus’s inability to master the art of the haggle leads Daisy to a negotiation with the attractive Ben, only to discover she may be flirting with the enemy. Meanwhile, at Oakley, disaster hits when Rowan, Julian and Paige wreak havoc, and the reaction from a livid Louis leads Julian to a rash decision. Louis seeks advice from Daisy on how to repair his relationship with Simone, only to disregard it after further conversation with Gus. Full of high hopes, he plans a grand gesture but doesn’t receive the response he hopes for. Don offers Louis the drunken advice of an unwise man, which leads to an intoxicated declaration. And a conversation with Julian yields information that surprises Daisy, leading her to offer relationship advice to Simone, which leaves Louis less than impressed.

programme.title: Sicily: The Wonder of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Historian Michael Scott begins his journey through Sicily on the slopes of Mount Etna, Europe's largest active volcano. For the ancient Greeks, the island was a land of gods and monsters - a dangerous and unpredictable world. Michael discovers how 3,000 years ago, the Greeks began to settle on Sicily's east coast - planting their olives and vines and building great city-states that soon came to rival even Athens itself. He learns how great battles were fought between the Greeks and the Carthaginians for control of the island. How the Romans made it their first foreign colony and stripped Sicily of its forests to plant vast fields of grain. When Rome fell, waves of Barbarian invasions followed, before Sicily was conquered by the Byzantines - the eastern Roman Empire. How have those early invaders helped to shape the character of the island we see today? And what lessons have Sicilians learnt from their turbulent past?

programme.title: Giorraíonn Beirt Bóthar
programme.desc: Siúlann Tessa Fleming agus Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill an bealach ársa ó Dhún Dealgan go hArd Mhacha. Tosaíonn siad ag Cuan Dhún Dealgan, agus buaileann siad isteach ar chaisleán Chú Chulainn. Tugann siad aghaidh ar thobar beannaithe Bhríde i bhFochaird, agus tugann siad sos dá gcosa le turas ar rothair tríd Bhealach an Mhaighre. Buaileann siad leis an ghrúpa siúlóide Sunrise Social, agus foghlamaíonn siad faoi stair fhada shaibhir Sheaneaglaisí Chill Shléibhe ar fhánaí Shliabh gCuillinn. Tessa Fleming and Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill travel the ancient route from Dundalk to Armagh. Beginning at Dundalk Bay, they call in at the legendary Cú Chulainn’s Castle before setting out towards St Brigid’s holy well at Faughart. Swapping their hiking boots for bicycles, they explore the Gap of the North, meet up with the Sunrise Social walking group and discover the enduring history of Killeavy Old Churches on the slopes of Slieve Gullion.

Full of high hopes, he plans a grand gesture but doesn’t receive the response he hopes for. Don offers Louis the drunken advice of an unwise man, which leads to an intoxicated declaration. And a conversation with Julian yields information that surprises Daisy, leading her to offer relationship advice to Simone, which leaves Louis less than impressed.

programme.title: Sicily: The Wonder of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Historian Michael Scott begins his journey through Sicily on the slopes of Mount Etna, Europe's largest active volcano. For the ancient Greeks, the island was a land of gods and monsters - a dangerous and unpredictable world. Michael discovers how 3,000 years ago, the Greeks began to settle on Sicily's east coast - planting their olives and vines and building great city-states that soon came to rival even Athens itself. He learns how great battles were fought between the Greeks and the Carthaginians for control of the island. How the Romans made it their first foreign colony and stripped Sicily of its forests to plant vast fields of grain. When Rome fell, waves of Barbarian invasions followed, before Sicily was conquered by the Byzantines - the eastern Roman Empire. How have those early invaders helped to shape the character of the island we see today? And what lessons have Sicilians learnt from their turbulent past?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. This show comes from Tidworth in Wiltshire, where fascinating finds include rare French porcelain, a regimental silver centrepiece, valuable toys and an unusual sardine tin.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: In Muncaster in Cumbria, hundreds of people turn up with collectibles and treasures they want to take to auction. Antiques experts James Lewis and Caroline Hawley uncover a few gems including a dazzling decanter and an art nouveau picture frame. Paul Martin visits Coniston Water in the Lake District.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael boards the Eurostar at London’s St Pancras International, bound for the Belgian capital, Brussels. In the city centre’s sumptuous Theatre Royal, he learns how an impassioned opera performance led to revolution on the streets and the birth of an independent nation. Travelling by tram to the residential district of Saint Gilles, Michael discovers the Belgian origins of art nouveau at the elegant house of architect Victor Horta. Finishing his first day at the headquarters of Nato, opened in 1967, he recalls his time as defence secretary and enjoys a private viewing of its impressive archive.

programme.title: Digging for Britain
programme.desc: In this special, Professor Alice Roberts reveals the forgotten story of the Roman Army's secret weapon in Britain - their cavalry. These fearsome horsemen were the key to defending Britain's most famous Roman monument fortification, Hadrian's Wall. Alice sets off across Hadrian's Wall to investigate any evidence the Roman cavalry left behind, while a team of archaeologists and historical re-enactors attempt to restage a Roman cavalry tournament - a spectacle that no-one has seen for over 1,600 years. We follow the team's training as they prepare for the performance, and Alice joins them at a public display in Carlisle where 30 riders perform in front of a crowd of spectators. To put the cavalry's story in context, the film also explores the latest archaeological digs happening across the UK, each of which is searching for new evidence of the Roman cavalry. On her journey across Hadrian's Wall, Alice visits some of the most iconic sites associated with the Roman cavalry, including Chester's Roman fort, Vindolanda fort and museum and Hexham Abbey. Along the way she builds a picture of the horsemen's lives here on the northern frontier of the Roman Empire.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Springwatch returns for three weeks of seasonal splendour. Broadcasting live from the brand new location of National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland, Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan deliver all the wildlife drama spring has to offer. With remote cameras rigged across the site, they uncover stories unfolding in real time. Iolo Williams undertakes his own wildlife wanderings, broadcasting live from the Knepp Estate in Sussex, where wildlife is thriving and ‘stand-out’ species are returning to the landscape.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Lucy explores how the battle for American independence wasn’t only fought on American soil but also unfolded in Britain itself, with sabotage, espionage and political unrest reshaping the empire. She reflects on a revolution that created an independent America but which also reshaped Britain and its monarchy.

programme.title: Giorraíonn Beirt Bóthar
programme.desc: Siúlann Tessa Fleming agus Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill an bealach ársa ó Dhún Dealgan go hArd Mhacha. Tosaíonn siad ag Cuan Dhún Dealgan, agus buaileann siad isteach ar chaisleán Chú Chulainn. Tugann siad aghaidh ar thobar beannaithe Bhríde i bhFochaird, agus tugann siad sos dá gcosa le turas ar rothair tríd Bhealach an Mhaighre. Buaileann siad leis an ghrúpa siúlóide Sunrise Social, agus foghlamaíonn siad faoi stair fhada shaibhir Sheaneaglaisí Chill Shléibhe ar fhánaí Shliabh gCuillinn. Tessa Fleming and Cormac Ó hÁdhmaill travel the ancient route from Dundalk to Armagh. Beginning at Dundalk Bay, they call in at the legendary Cú Chulainn’s Castle before setting out towards St Brigid’s holy well at Faughart. Swapping their hiking boots for bicycles, they explore the Gap of the North, meet up with the Sunrise Social walking group and discover the enduring history of Killeavy Old Churches on the slopes of Slieve Gullion.

programme.title: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret.
programme.desc: Eleven-year-old Margaret is uprooted from her life in New York City for the suburbs of New Jersey, going through the messy and tumultuous throes of puberty with new friends in a new school. She relies on her mother, Barbara, who is also struggling to adjust to life outside the big city, and her adoring grandmother, Sylvia, who isn’t happy they moved away and likes to remind them every chance she gets. Based on Judy Blume’s classic novel.

programme.title: Joins BBC News
programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: After more than 11,000km across eight countries, the teams face one final test of endurance as they race to claim victory at the finish line in Hatgal, Mongolia.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve and a team of world-class kayakers head to the Kamchatka Peninsula in the far east of Russia to take on the first descent of the Kronotsky River – through white water so extreme that it has never before been attempted. The team set out to paddle from source to sea, starting in the shadow of a still-active volcano and ending at the Pacific Ocean – kayaking through an unspoilt wilderness packed with more brown bears than almost anywhere else on the planet. If the team can make it through the white water, they will enter an untouched landscape and witness brown bears in their natural habitat, unaffected by humans. These Russian brown bears are so isolated, some of them may never have seen people before.

programme.title: The Cage
programme.desc: As forces close in on Matty and Leanne, and the evidence stacks up against them, can they pull off one last roll of the dice?

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin lead the search along with guest judge and keen gardener Katie Piper to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. Up first is Colin’s surprising suburban rustic garden in suburban Ballymena. In the foothills of the Sperrin Mountains, near the windswept Glenshane Pass, Adrienne has transformed two acres using a variety of planting styles. The final stop is in Dromore, where Julietta has created a garden designed with her young family very much in mind, including a wild meadow playground and a courtyard filled with edible plants. There are mixed opinions at the judging table – so which will expert judges Diarmuid, Carol and Katie feel deserves a place in the Greatest Garden final?

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: In this special episode of Deadly 60, Steve Backshall takes a deep dive into the fate of one of the most extraordinary, and endangered, ecosystems on our planet: coral reefs. They may cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, but they support roughly a quarter of all marine life and are irreplaceable - yet they are in serious trouble. Steve travels to some of the world’s most celebrated reef systems, from the shallows of the Java Sea to the tropical waters of the Maldives. Along the way, he meets all the weird and wonderful creatures that call the reef home, including some of the best-camouflaged creatures and some impressive apex predators - he even gets a telling-off from a clownfish!

programme.title: My Life
programme.desc: Twelve-year-old Laleeyah lives on the Crow Creek Native American reservation in South Dakota, USA. There aren’t many opportunities for people on the reservation, and life can be tough, but Laleeyah loves to learn about the traditions of her ancestors and takes pride in keeping them alive. Once a year there is the Pow Wow: a big, colourful, celebration where the whole Crow Creek tribe comes together to compete and celebrate with traditional dancing, music and dress. For several years running Laleeyah has been crowned Junior Miss Crow Creek - the best young dancer on the reservation. But since the last Pow Wow she has developed an illness called hyperthyroidism, which makes her feel weak and tired. As she comes to terms with her illness, Laleeyah still wants to hold on to the things she loves most: dancing, representing her tribe, and her crown. But will she have what it takes, and can she still be the dancing queen?

Steve travels to some of the world’s most celebrated reef systems, from the shallows of the Java Sea to the tropical waters of the Maldives. programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends host a summer party and pick vegetables to make a delicious salad. Mr Tumble’s also hosting a party, but he struggles to find a garden game that he’s good at.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po follow a trail of flowers that leads them to some very special treasure.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how Scots pine trees play an important role in the environment. They find out that they can help improve habitats for plants and animals and that their rough bark is a great place for insects to hide from predators. They learn that wood from these trees can be used to build homes and furniture and that wood ants can use its pine needles to make their homes too. On the way, they spot a red squirrel out looking for seeds to eat.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Taran pretends his favourite teddy doesn’t belong to him, but when it goes missing, he gets upset. The Fantastics go on a bear hunt, and Taran realises he is not too old for teddies.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that all help build things. Grace uses a road roller to flatten a road, shows off a giant bucket-wheel excavator and then uses a telescopic loader to move some bricks up high.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: It's Kindness Day, and the pups notice that Puggers is not being himself. The pups try various acts of kindness to cheer him up.

programme.title: Vegesaurs

programme.title: Peter Rabbit

programme.title: Hey Duggee

Duggee was a great dancer, but he never stuck to the choreography and was always making up his own moves.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Zog is too scared to fly after a bad crash landing, so Boom helps the doctors as their ambulance. Zog must overcome his fear and get back to the team.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: On Big Fix Day, Ava’s Good-As-New machine repairs everything - even things that don’t need mending. But when it fails, she has to find another way to fix the children’s toys.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Simon and Waffle are home alone. Simon recalls the first time he met Waffle as a pup, and the pair share memories of the Wonder Dog becoming part of the Brooklyn-Bell family.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: At the bring-and-buy sale, Rafi insists on keeping her oldest toy, Tommy the T rex. But after a busy day, she realises he’s gone. Worried, she makes a wish to find him, and her wishing wand whisks her and Jake on a wild chase through the park. Finally, back at the bakery, they discover baby Oscar happily playing with Tommy - Amy bought it to cheer him up. Seeing Oscar’s joy, Rafi decides to let him keep Tommy.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo wants to go somewhere new, so Gran Gran takes her to discover new places in the local community. They visit Jared's shop, the community garden and the roof of the library, spotting lots of new things along the way. JoJo realises that even when you think you know somewhere, there are always new places to discover.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. A sleepy Sarah attempts to bake a dessert for a hungry Duck.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Out fishing in the music boat, Small catches a strange-looking object. He doesn't know what it is, but he thinks Tiny might like it, so he gives it to her as a present. At first she is really pleased and puts it in her bedcave. But when she tries to get to sleep, it makes strange shadows on the wall and becomes rather scary. Tiny decides she must get rid of it. But this is not as simple a job as it sounds! Wherever she puts it, it has a mysterious habit of coming back to her bedcave...

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo loves dancing. BaBa wants to dance but finds it hard to follow MeMo’s steps. At the Play Tree, they choose a music speaker and do some more dancing. BaBa is still struggling to copy MeMo’s routine and decides to watch MeMo dance instead. At Yummy Time, the Yummies show BaBa that there are many different ways to dance. BaBa joins in, doing their own BaBa dance. BaBa loves dancing too.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Upsy Daisy has a dancey day in the garden. First she bops with the Tombliboos and then she dances with the Pontipines. Igglepiggle and Upsy Daisy dance together before everybody joins in at the gazebo.

programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the bagpipe-playing Chilli Peppers, melting Kiwi backstage and performing their song We’re Chilli When It’s Hot!.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula find a helium balloon stuck in a tree in the park. They both want to play with it at the same time, so Flop makes two strings and they invent a noisy balloon game called stuck duckies. When they run in opposite directions, the balloon flies away, and Flop volunteers to be the stuck duckie so the game doesn't have to end.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Po needs an extra snooze before waking up for an energetic Tubby Phone dance. In Tummy Tales, children enjoy acting out the nursery song Sleeping Bunnies.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Preschool animation. A day out in the park shows Tee that it can be more fun to share the playground rides with his friends than to always go first.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Carrot is excited to show the Tato Team her new inventions, including an improved Robotato, who will help them protect the supermarket from Evil Pea. Unfortunately, Robotato still has a few glitches, so the veggies decide to test Carrot's new jetpacks instead, but Evil Pea sneaks in and commands Robotato to protect her. When Robotato continues to glitch, he becomes overly protective of Evil Pea and takes her to the top of Tato Tower to keep her safe. The Tato Team, led by the real Supertato, must use their new jetpacks to fly up and save her.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Pando is teaching Bing and Sula how to do little kicks and big kicks with a ball in the garden. Sula does the biggest kick of them all, but Bing kicks the ball the wrong way. As he tries to kick it back to Pando it bounces off the shed, breaking Flop's window! They have to stand statue-still while Flop cleans up the glass.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Everyone wants to win Swoppiton’s hide-and-seek tournament. But Mojo and Bo accidentally break the prize. They need to put it back together without the seeker spotting them!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It’s a right royal do today, as we are introduced by King Tiger himself, along with a Jelly Belly dancer who doesn’t say much but instead expresses themselves through the medium of wobbling. We start by joining Tag in the kitchen, who wants a snack, then it’s time for the first question of the day from a bunny: why does Nigel Crab not say anything? Little Bug and Bear have questions too. At juice time, Happy can’t help noticing something different about Norrie. She's had a haircut and talks about the very first time she went to the hairdresser. There’s a tooting good dot-to-dot featuring our favourite elephant, and then it’s Enid’s time to shine in a musical caper.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are excited to learn that Mr Wobbly, the jelly juggler, is coming to town, and they can’t wait to see him. But they become impatient, so Duggee makes sure to explain to them that the week will fly by and there’s a lot to be done in that time. Duggee explains that a week is made up of seven days and what activities he does each day to stay busy. Each squirrel excitedly shares their usual plans between Monday and Friday so that they have something to look forward to while they wait for Mr Wobbly’s arrival.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Indy’s upset her model horse looks like a cow, but Calypso encourages her not to give up.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo and Bluey want Mum and Dad to smoochy kiss, so they set up a romantic evening for two at their fancy restaurant. Everything goes to plan, until Chef Bingo’s special arrives.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch makes popcorn in Mount Etna, blocking the volcano and endangering the farms on its slopes.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter forgets to get his mother a present for Mother's Day, his hurried attempts to put things right lead to adventure.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. A timid sperm whale must conquer his fears and dive deep down to help the Octonauts release Peso from a giant clam.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The number friends all want to do different things today, so rocket Ten finds a clever way to do them all. Learn all the ways to add to ten with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The Alphablocks meet their match when Brown Cow and her singing friends Owl, Howl and Growl take the stage! This episode has fun with the '-ow-' digraph and the words cow, brown, owl, howl, growl, gown, crown, town and down.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Today is the Popavision Song Contest, and Nick and Norman think they can win it. With the Popcast Planners and Nick’s Popavison costume, the stage is set for an exciting evening, But what song should they sing?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels go on a bus ride with Duggee as they sing 'Wheels on the Bus'.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella is busy gardening, but Lift isn’t happy that she is making a mess with all that mud! Together, they set off to explore the floors of Playtime Towers. In the Cloud Kitchen, Patch makes a tasty treat with the Playtimers - Munchy Muddy Meadows, whilst in the Sing Song Forest, lots of muddy pictures are appearing in Tincy’s wondiferous web. In the Fortress of Fun, Kingsley and Queenie have a fun idea to play a game with the Playtimers called ‘The Muddy Pig Race’, but who will win, Team King or Team Queen?

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing wants to try Coco's hula hoop. It's harder than it looks, but they all find lots of other hoopy games on the way. Just as Bing almost gets it right, he gets carried away with spinning and breaks the hoop. Coco is upset she can't hula anymore - until Bing and Charlie remind her of all the other games they can still do with the bent hoop.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say 'top', and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see a red top, a blue top and a new top. There’s a soft top, a scratchy top, and Dee and a friend discover they have matchy tops. We meet a cool top, see lots of kids in school tops, and there’s even a tiger top!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu struggles to find any treasure during a trip to the park.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri and Lou decide to take Pania a giant fruit as a present. But as they bring it to her, they can’t resist having a taste of it - and another, and another...

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: When Alex sets up a tent, the Froglets head into the desert as ancient pyramid explorers.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in an artist's studio, where they watch a painter preparing to start work on a huge canvas laid out on the floor. He accidentally kicks a pot of paint, emptying its contents onto the canvas, and in trying to clear up the spilled paint he falls and gets covered in it. When he leaves to get cleaned up, the Twirlywoos decide to tip out more pots onto the canvas, as well as squeezing the contents out of tubes, until the canvas is covered in different coloured paint. The artist returns and is surprised and pleased with the new painting. The Stop-Go Car visits the boat, and this time when it opens its boot, a huge inflatable beach ball comes out! The ball bounces around the boat, while the Twirlywoos try to stay out of its way. Finally, Peekaboo heads the ball and sends it sailing right out of the door.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Ben meets Hussain and Hassan at a garden to learn about insects. They pretend to be bees and explore a bug hotel. Mr Tumble is in amongst the flowers trying to make friends with a bee. There's an arty spotty surprise making boingy butterflies. Featuring signs for the words bee, insect and caterpillar.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy and Laa-Laa follow a trail of muddy footprints and find Po in bed with very muddy feet. The Noo-noo cleans off the mud.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Evie, Gracie, Luke, Joseph, Thea, Benjamin and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are eggboxes which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate eggboxes inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song Humpty Dumpty features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children build a pretend sleepover den, learn British Sign Language signs for brother, sleeping and morning, then sing and sign Frère Jacques.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Novah and Joda go on a springtime adventure, meeting a beatboxing daffodil to find out why all the plants are starting to wake up.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Murphi thinks he has seen an alien in the attic, but it’s only Rebecca pretending to be an underwater ocean explorer. Water inspires the first monster make of the day – a sea turtle bowl. The Mini Monsters are inspired by water too, transforming different-shaped boxes into boats. Rebecca’s cousin is by the sea, turning discarded rubbish from the beach into a fantastic seascape. Finally, Rebecca and Murphi create a manta ray from an old plastic bottle, with the Tiny Helpers lending a hand.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and her friends must use all their clever thinking to open fossilised honeysuckle.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Playing 'Shops' is the best game ever for Bluey and her friends - if they can ever get started! With Bluey questioning the rules and changing who's who, they might be here all day!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After overhearing Duggee listening to a beautiful track by the Squirrel Valley Voices Choir, the Squirrels seek to learn more about the roles that make up a choir – basses, sopranos, altos and tenors. A distressed Eugene then alerts them that half of the choir have been taken sick and can’t perform that day. The Squirrels step up to take their place. Initially, when the newly arranged choir sing, the voices aren’t gelling together. Duggee teaches them the principles they must get right first, for the choir to succeed – breathing, pitch, volume, focus and timing. With a lot of practice, the Squirrels turn up to perform perfectly together and finally earn their Choir Badge.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Come and join the number jam - it's counting with Duggee!

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to a great place to draw some pictures using charcoal. On the way they spin like windmills, visit the burnt forest, climb a tree and even run from a dinosaur!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Ted and his family visit a wildlife park, and Ted gets to be an animal keeper for the day. First, he feeds the hungry deer. They’re very friendly. Next, it’s onto the bison, who show Ted their giant tongues! Finally, Ted comes face to face with a very noisy and very hungry otter. Luckily, Ted speaks otter too!

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Marian is making gyuveche today, and before his friends arrive they taste one of the main ingredients – feta cheese. They don't all like it at first, so let’s hope they change their minds when they taste the finished dish. Marian works hard layering peppers, tomatoes and feta in beautiful Bulgarian pots. He then puts an egg on top of each one before it cooks in the oven. When his friends arrive, Marian is wearing traditional national dress and gives them all a traditional bracelet as a gift.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today’s episode Maddie is going high and low! She takes her special 360 camera to the top of the longest suspension bridge in the UK to find out how it works. Maddie discovers a suspension bridge has really strong cables that use forces to carry all the people and traffic across the river, and she heads underground to see how the cables are buried. Next, Maddie heads to a playground flooring factory to see how different materials are mixed together, creating a chemical reaction, and melted into a gloopy mixture to make a dolphin shape at a playground.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Dan and Jamie head for the hills to earn their compass badge searching for some missing ramblers and their teachers.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some dholes. These are wild dogs that live across Asia, from China to Thailand, as well as in the dense forests of India. Also known as the whistling dog, they produce whistling calls to coordinate the pack when they are hunting. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet some dwarf mongooses. They can live in groups of up to 30 and are tiny - about half the size of a rabbit. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Evie finishes her reading book before school, so she can hand it in and bring a new book home later. Home alone, Waffle makes up a chant and dances around the house to the music. He spots Evie’s reading book! She’s accidentally left it behind and it needs to be handed in today. Waffle doesn’t know what to do. He could take the book to Evie, but he’s banned from school...

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona makes a friend – forever!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: The garden gang compete in a three-legged race. Stripes struggles until he finds his three-legged rhythm.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are off to the bowling alley with Mum and Dad. Everyone else is knocking down pins, but poor Dad just can’t catch a break. Time to focus! Can Maddie and Triggs help Dad find his bowling groove and get that elusive strike, or will he be left in the gutter?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: King Tiger interrupts the Squirrels' quiet time when he turns up at the Clubhouse with a magic hat on instead of his crown. He puts on a magic show for the Squirrels, making things appear and disappear to enthusiastic requests.

programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A secret advantage is won, and when its existence becomes clear, is Billy about to be exposed?

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. The second player is removed from the game, but relief is short-lived as the group realises a potentially more dangerous liar remains. A playful garden party game exposes the gaps in some of the group’s popular culture knowledge. With pressure mounting, one player’s guilt takes over, and he starts to question whether to continue in the game. The house regroups, but trust is thin. A secret advantage is won, and when its existence becomes clear, is Billy about to be exposed?

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

That night, a teenager is found dead at the bottom of the stairs - when it's clear the local police won't give these 'broken' children a proper investigation, Alphy calls Geordie. DCI Gill Murray and DC Rachel Bailey go to Bristol to advise on a rape and murder case which bears striking similarities to an infamous case from 13 years ago. At the time of the original case, Gill helped catch the perpetrator Jeremy Leach, who was convicted for the rape and murder of four women but is now claiming that he is innocent. Another woman has been raped and killed using Leach's exact MO; could the real murderer still be out there? At home, Rachel discovers that her brother Dom is prostituting himself in her flat. She is furious and also heartbroken to realise that this is how Dom got by in prison. Later, Rachel learns that the CPS will not be charging her ex-boyfriend Nick Savage with her attempted murder. programme.title: Rentadick
programme.desc: 1972. Comedy. Director: Jim Clark. Stars James Booth, Richard Briers & Julie Ege. The incompetent detectives of Rentadick Inc track thieves of a nerve gas that paralyses from the waist down.

programme.title: The Rogues
programme.desc: Gambit By The Golden Gate. 1965. Gig Young, David Niven and Charles Boyer are The Rogues, members of two related families of international forgers and conmen. [S]

programme.title: The Adventures of Robin Hood
programme.desc: Richard The Lionheart. 1956. Stars Richard Greene, Victor Woolf & Archie Duncan. Arriving back in England King Richard is in disguise. Who can he count on for loyalty? [S]

programme.title: The Buccaneers
programme.desc: The Return of Calico Jack. 1957. Stars Brian Worth, Jan Miller & Anne Blake. Calico Jack arrives in the colony while Tempest is away on business, resulting in tension between the two crews. [S]

programme.title: William Tell
programme.desc: The Shrew. 1959. Stars: Conrad Phillips, Willoughby Goddard & Jennifer Jayne. Hedda, lured away by a message that her sister is ill, finds herself an unwilling pawn in Gessler's latest plot. [S]

programme.title: The Vise
programme.desc: Death Pays No Dividends. 1954. Stars Eunice Gayson, Peter Reynolds & John Warwick. To fund their lavish lifestyle a playboy and his girlfriend plot to swindle money out of an insurance company. [S]

programme.title: Circumstantial Evidence (1952)
programme.desc: 1952. Crime. Director: Daniel Birt. Stars: Rona Anderson, Patrick Holt & John Arnatt. Cleverly crafted crime drama - A woman seeks evidence that will give her grounds for divorce. [S]

programme.title: The Atomic Submarine
programme.desc: 1959. Sci-fi. Directed by Spencer Gordon Bennet. Stars Arthur Franz & Dick Foran. A submarine is sent out to investigate a series of naval disasters, but the crew also get caught up in the chaos. [S]

programme.title: Look At Life Air Hostess
programme.desc: 1964. A Look into an airline stewardess during her working day.

programme.title: The Small Back Room
programme.desc: 1949. Drama. Directors Michael Powell, Emeric Pressburger. Stars David Farrar, Jack Hawkins and Kathleen Byron. The best bomb disposal expert must battle his inner self, during the German raids. [S]

programme.title: Star Performance
programme.desc: 1954. Drama. Directed by William Cameron Menzies. Stars Ronald Colman, Angela Lansbury & Brenda Forbes. A woman's life changes when a gem expert declares the string of beads she wears is valuable. [S]

programme.title: Sergeant Cork
programme.desc: The Case of the Ormsby Diamonds. 1964. Stars John Barrie, William Gaunt & Edward Woodward. Diamonds are stolen from the Ormsby family, could a family member or guest have taken them? [S]

programme.title: Richard the Lionheart
programme.desc: The Challenge. 1962. Stars Dermot Walsh, Zena Marshall & Trader Faulkner. Richard is challenged by Zara, Princess of Granada, into a joust with her brother, Ubaldo, with her as the prize. [S]

programme.title: Whispering Smith Hits London
programme.desc: 1952. Mystery. Director: Francis Searle. Stars Richard Carlson, Greta Gynt & Herbert Lom. US sleuth Whispering Smith arrives in London on holiday but soon becomes embroiled in a murder case. [S]

programme.title: The Long Duel
programme.desc: 1967. Drama. Director: Ken Annakin. Stars Yul Brynner, Trevor Howard, Harry Andrews. A police officer is sent to capture a rebel leader who threatens the stability of Raj's northwest frontier. [S]

programme.title: The Directors
programme.desc: Fritz Lang began in Germany with Metropolis and M. He then built a new career following the Nazi uprising, moving to Hollywood to become the king of film noir. [S]

programme.title: The Veil
programme.desc: The Doctor. 1958. Stars Boris Karloff, Katherine Squire & Peter Miller. A young surgeon is denied permission to operate on a dying girl, eerie questions arise about trust and second chances. [S]

programme.title: The Footage Detectives
programme.desc: Enjoy exclusive and rare footage from the 1968 premiere of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang featuring Dick Van Dyke, as well as a great reel of Melbourne's street cleaners in 1964. [S]

programme.title: Maigret
programme.desc: Maigret and the Burglar's Wife. 1991. Stars Bruno Cremer, Michael Lonsdale & Renée Faure. A murder has occurred during a burglary at a dentist's home, but no one wants to cooperate with Maigret. [S]

programme.title: The Quatermass Xperiment
programme.desc: 1955. Horror. Director: Val Guest. Stars Brian Donlevy, Jack Warner & Thora Hird. A manned rocket ship returns to Earth with two astronauts missing and the survivor incapable of communicating. [S]

programme.title: The Lawless Years
programme.desc: The Nick Joseph Story. 1959. Stars James Gregory, Vic Morrow & Jan Merlin. Ruditsky flips an ex-con to expose a new racketeering play.

programme.title: Murder East, Murder West
programme.desc: 1990. Thriller. Directed by Peter Smith. Stars Jeroen Krabbé, Suzanna Hamilton & Joanna Pearce. A crook finds his past catching up with him in the shape of the ex-girlfriend he thought was dead.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.
